name: Bridging the Gap (Application)

objectives.text: Name one thing a short Bible passage tells God's people to do
Give an example of how a child could obey a Bible command at home or at school
Explain that the Bible was written long ago yet still teaches God's people today
Describe how the example of Jesus in a Gospel story shows his followers how to live
Summarize the difference between what a passage meant to its first hearers and what it teaches readers today
Explain why a reader must understand what a passage means before deciding how to apply it
Explain how ordinary activities such as eating, work, and schoolwork can be done for the glory of God
Compare a cultural custom in a Bible passage with the lasting principle it expresses
Classify whether a passage calls mainly for a change in belief, attitude, or action
Apply the principle of a passage to a specific situation in school or family life
Analyze a passage by stating its original meaning, the timeless principle it teaches, and a present-day application
Use the Westminster Larger Catechism rules for the commandments to identify the duties and sins implied by a single commandment
Distinguish commands tied to a particular cultural or covenant setting from commands that bind in every age using evidence from the text
Explain how the Bible's statements about who believers are in Christ ground the commands that follow them
Contrast legalistic and lawless applications of a passage and explain how each departs from Scripture
Analyze how Christ's fulfillment of the Old Testament shapes the way an Old Testament passage is applied today
Construct a faithful application of an ancient text for a specific present-day cultural setting
Evaluate a modern ethical dilemma using principles drawn from Scripture read in context
Defend the relevance of the Old Testament for Christian living using New Testament teaching
Evaluate a published devotional or sermon for whether its application is faithful to the meaning of its passage
Produce a devotional or sermon outline that applies a text to a specific audience

changes: Removed the Jude 4 citation entirely. Reworded the K item so it no longer centres on the student's personal sense of God's will, and reworded the 'be like Jesus' item into an observable description of Christ's example. Kept and sharpened the then/now, understand-before-apply, custom-versus-principle, principlizing, cultural-versus-universal, indicative-imperative, legalism, construct, ethics, Old Testament relevance, and sermon outline competencies. Expanded the legalism item to include the opposite error of lawlessness. Added competencies on doing ordinary work for God's glory, classifying the kind of change a passage calls for, the Larger Catechism rules for the commandments, Christ's fulfillment shaping Old Testament application, and evaluating published applications. Anchored items to specific verses and to Westminster and Heidelberg articles where they state the doctrine.
